hypothesis: Factor concentration: a high52-only book (pred = factor_high52 z-score) beats the 7-factor blend under the identical production construction grid. Pre-registered as a follow-up to the factor report card, which showed high52 as the only factor with positive dev IC, monotonic deciles and a net-of-cost spread on the corrected ruler.
rule: dev decides, holdout must confirm direction (surv panel is the evaluation standard; full panel reported for completeness).
verdict: REJECTED on the standard (surv) ruler: dev improves (0.37-0.46 vs 0.22-0.36) but holdout flips negative. Mechanism, consistent with the factor card: the blend's holdout is carried by the volatility factor (holdout IC +0.051, monotonic deciles there), its dev by high52 -- the two factors lead in different regimes and the blend's diversification across them is real work, not noise. Concentration discards it.
watch: On the full (501-name) panel the high52-only book is the most balanced configuration seen (dev 0.25-0.30, holdout 0.87-1.09) while the blend collapses in dev. Single holdout window; logged for the November review alongside the high52 removal trigger and the accruals watch-list. No production change.
implication_for_weighting: The concern that volatility's 28.8% weight was 'a recent run' is only half right: its holdout contribution is real. Re-weighting on dev-period IC alone would remove exactly the factor that carried the holdout. Any weighting change must be judged on both segments.
